verification_scope: Recovered bibliographic records and historical evidence roles; not a fresh systematic review or full-text verification. Original downloaded/missing-full-text status remains in references/literature/manifest.json.

records.title: Multiple resources and mental workload
records.role: Parallel tasks may compete for shared processing resources.
records.limits: A theoretical lens, not a measurement of this study's participants.

records.title: Interaction in 4-second bursts: The fragmented nature of attentional resources in mobile HCI
records.role: Urban mobile interaction involves fragmented attention.
records.limits: The original tasks were not identical to this walking-navigation protocol.

records.title: Using spontaneous eye blink-related brain activity to investigate cognitive load during mobile map-assisted navigation
records.role: Map information conditions involve trade-offs in a controlled virtual-navigation study.
records.limits: No universal landmark-count rule; interviews do not measure the same physiological indicators.

records.title: It's also about timing! When do pedestrians want to receive navigation instructions
records.role: Instruction timing is relevant to pedestrian navigation information.
records.limits: Does not validate the group's proposed information categories.

records.title: PocketNavigator: Studying tactile navigation systems in-situ
records.role: Alternative delivery channels can change interaction with navigation information.
records.limits: Reduced screen interaction is not itself proof of reduced cognitive load.

records.title: Association between smartphone glances during application-based navigation and pedestrian navigation performance: A real-world experimental study
records.role: Supports examining phone glances, stops, errors and their sequence.
records.limits: Associations do not establish causation or an overwhelmed experience.

records.title: Visitors' wayfinding strategies and navigational aids in unfamiliar urban environment
records.role: Digital navigation, strategies and unfamiliar-city experience need to be distinguished.
records.limits: Do not generalise a single setting to all newcomers or infer energy depletion.

records.title: Finding your way: Exploring urban park users' engagement with a wayfinding intervention through intercept go-along interviews
records.role: Wayfinding information can support perceived manageability and exploration confidence.
records.limits: Park users are not the same population or task as this study.

records.title: Situationally-induced impairments and disabilities
records.role: Contextual conditions may constrain technology use.
records.limits: Does not directly establish the effect of a navigation design.

records.title: Unlocking context-aware mobile map adaptation
records.role: Context and map-content adaptation complicate simple information-reduction rules.
records.limits: Historical verification covered publication metadata and summaries; no new full-text reading claimed.

records.title: Learning to use transit services
records.role: Unfamiliar transit use provides neighbouring qualitative experience evidence.
records.limits: Transit evidence does not establish the full causal chain for Hong Kong walking.

records.title: Wayfinding strategies and tourist anxiety in unfamiliar destinations
records.role: Links perceived wayfinding difficulty with anxiety in a tourism setting.
records.limits: Association and contextual difference limit transfer.

records.title: Pedestrian navigation aids: Information requirements and design implications
records.role: Separates instruction purpose from importance and redundancy.
records.limits: Historical discussion described author-uploaded text; the framework is not this group's final taxonomy.

records.title: Orientation information in wayfinding instructions: evidences from human verbal and visual instructions
records.role: Orientation information can be distinguished from action information.
records.limits: Source use is preserved from the earlier discussion, not freshly verified.

records.title: Understanding information requirements in "text only" pedestrian wayfinding systems
records.limits: Earlier verification was an institutional-repository abstract, not a full reading.

records.title: Research methods in human-computer interaction (2nd ed.)
records.role: Case protocols, observation, interviews and qualitative analysis.
records.limits: Method guidance does not prescribe the group's exact sample or duration.

records.title: Looking back: Retrospective study methods for HCI
records.limits: Recall can be uncertain and does not prove an internal mechanism.

records.title: Eye tracking: A brief introduction
records.role: A precedent discussed for practice tasks.
records.limits: The walking warm-up is the group's adaptation, not an eye-tracking replication.
